trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access to electronic data containing personal information) of Florida residents. The custom records are treated as personal information because of the 2026 geolocation element (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VII)); counsel confirms
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 additional days only if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after determination (501.171(3)(a); applies to this individual notice only)
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email, with the date range, the information involved, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - treated as applying (about 640 individuals in the records); counsel confirms the geolocation reading

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with a synopsis, the number affected, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents are affected (possible: about 640 in the records)

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the shop reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Determination documented in writing and kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - possible, because the records hold no Social Security, license, or account numbers; counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Notice to individuals delayed for the period the agency's written request specifies
notify: Hold the individual notice; keep the written request

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: No at the current record count (about 640); recheck if the records pass 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the shop (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes the shop's personal information (email and file provider, booking form vendor) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination; the shop then gives the notices above
notify: The shop (owner-operator), at the security contact registered with each vendor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track vendor notices; the shop's own 30-day clock starts on receipt

trigger: Affected customers who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residence of affected customers (nearly all live in Florida)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Card processor notice of suspected card reader compromise
citation: Merchant agreement (contract); Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1.1
trigger: Card reader or the phone it pairs with is lost, stolen, or suspected compromised
deadline: Per merchant terms (time not set in this sample; promptly). Whatever the agreement says, Visa's rules require the compromise to be reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation, through the processor (What To Do If Compromised v10.0, A.1.1)
verified: n/a (contract term not set); true (Visa clock)

applies_at_this_tier: Only if coverage exists - no standalone cyber policy; check the business liability policy for a cyber endorsement

obligation: Customer notice of held or unsafe product
trigger: Product whose temperature, cook program, or cure amount may have been affected
deadline: Before the owner of the animal picks up the product; same day if pickup is scheduled
notify: Each affected livestock or product owner, by phone
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the shop's own duty to its customers; custom product must not be adulterated (9 CFR 303.1(b)(1))

obligation: FSIS notice of adulterated or misbranded product in commerce
trigger: Adulterated or misbranded product from an official establishment has entered commerce
applies_at_this_tier: No - written for official establishments; the shop is custom exempt. If an FSIS reviewer asks about an incident, records are shown under 9 CFR 300.6(b)(2)

trigger: Determination that an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: No later than 24 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the duty falls on registered food facilities; the shop is not registered (21 CFR 1.226(g))

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect) (C-FOOD-AG-R02)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, a food and agriculture entity below the SBA size standard is not covered

obligation: Reporting of cyber incidents at MTSA facilities (C-FOOD-AG-R03)
trigger: Actual or threatened cyber incident at an MTSA facility
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or the National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - the shop is not an MTSA facility

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the shop holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the shop holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
